customManagers.description: `rust-version` in Cargo.toml is the third copy of the toolchain release. Tracked as the `rust` Docker image so it uses the same `major.minor` versioning as the `rust:<version>-slim` base in the Dockerfile, and the `rust toolchain` group moves it with the other two.

packageRules.description: The Rust toolchain moves in one pull request: `channel` in rust-toolchain.toml, the `rust:<version>-slim` base image in the Dockerfile and `rust-version` in Cargo.toml name the same release, and apps/web/tests/toolchain_pins.rs fails if they drift apart. Digest updates (same release, rebuilt image) stay ungrouped.

Keeps the `rust toolchain` group whole while a member is inside `minimumReleaseAge`. Under the default `internalChecksFilter: strict`, Renovate drops pending updates from a branch that also holds ready ones, which is how a toolchain bump once shipped without its base image. `none` keeps every update in the branch and reports the pending age as the `renovate/stability-days` status; `platformAutomerge: false` hands the merge to Renovate, which waits for that status, where GitHub's native auto-merge only waits for required checks. Matched without `matchUpdateTypes`: Renovate reads `internalChecksFilter` before an update type exists, so a rule narrowed by update type never applies it.

Docker Hub stamps a tag with its last push, and the official `rust` images are rebuilt on every base image update, so `rust:<version>-slim` keeps looking days old or less long after the release. The toolchain member of the `rust toolchain` group carries the release age for the whole group; on the image it would only keep the group pending. Digest updates keep the age gate, because there the push is the change.
`rust-version` is a bare version, not an image reference: there is no digest to pin.
